A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Video2BEV research. All 14 pages of v3 and 16 pages of v4, including supplementary material, are readable, and corresponding methods, equations, tables and figures can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v3 reports original UniV retrieval experiments, SUES-200 transfer results, ablations and qualitative failure analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains those empirical results and adds rainy-weather testing, efficiency measurements, frame-rate experiments and trajectory-length visualizations.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 retain the BEV transformation, diffusion-generated negatives, encoder/MLP architecture, losses and two-stage reranking. The new optimized-renderer timing disclosure does not document revised localization steps or establish a change to the benchmarked model.

E1.justification: v4 adds a synthetic rainy-weather scenario on UniV, matching rain-corrupted drone data with clean satellite images (Section 9). The underlying datasets, locations, elevation-angle coverage and SUES-200 evaluation remain unchanged.

E2.justification: LPN, FSRA, DWDR and Sample4Geo remain the evaluated comparators. The new weather, efficiency and FPS comparisons use this same set; Speedy-Splat is cited as a rendering implementation, not added as a competing localization method.

E3.justification: Added evaluations compare rain augmentation before versus after BEV reconstruction, 2/5/10 FPS, and reconstructions from 18/36/54 frames. v4 also introduces parameter-count, GFLOP and ranking-latency measurements. Existing splits, training budgets and retrieval protocols are retained; identifying previous experiments as using 2 FPS is additional disclosure.

E4.justification: The appendix substantially expands diagnostic evidence through rain robustness and corruption-placement tests, FPS sensitivity, trajectory-length reconstruction comparisons and efficiency analysis. These examine previously untested reconstruction vulnerabilities and practical input requirements. Existing component, training-strategy, reranking, loss-weight and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests for these experiments. The added results retain point-estimate reporting.

E6.justification: Tables 2–3 and the retained loss-weight results are unchanged, but v4 adds substantive findings under new conditions. Rainy D→S AP is 33.75 with corruption before reconstruction and 67.49 with corruption afterward (Table 4). Video2BEV S→D AP is 96.57/96.21/95.42 at 2/5/10 FPS (Table 7). Table 5 adds 6.26 ms ranking latency, 215.26M parameters and 28.38 GFLOPs. The appendix changes the vanilla rendering bound from under 8 seconds to under 1 second and separately reports 0.15 seconds for optimized rendering.

T1.justification: The loss definitions in Equations (1)–(4) and the supplementary weighted-loss formulation are unchanged. No new formal assumptions, derivations, propositions or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: video-based drone localization, Video2BEV transformation, synthetic hard negatives and UniV. The headline UniV and SUES-200 performance claims are unchanged.

C2.justification: v4 attributes rainy-input failures to unreliable camera-pose and point-cloud reconstruction, discusses the remaining need for remote rendering, and emphasizes multiview coverage over FPS. These add applicability qualifications. The broad FPS-improvement discussion gives little attention to Video2BEV's mixed results in Table 7.

D1.justification: v4 adds a code-access link, identifies prior experiments as using 2 FPS and the default reconstruction input as 54 frames, and discloses optimized 3DGS timing on one RTX 4090. It revises the appendix's vanilla rendering-time bound while retaining the older bound in Section 4.1. It also removes the explicit PyTorch and multi-round-captioning disclosures without establishing corresponding implementation changes.

R1.justification: v4 adds Hanson et al.'s Speedy-Splat reference to support the optimized-rendering discussion. The other 79 cited works and the substantive related-work positioning are retained; most citation changes are renumbering.

P1.justification: The main narrative receives limited wording edits, revised author affiliations and contribution markings, and an acknowledgment section. The appendix outline and section hierarchy expand to accommodate the new analyses, while existing explanations largely remain intact.

P2.justification: v4 adds weather and trajectory Figures 12 and 14 and weather, efficiency and FPS Tables 4, 5 and 7. The old failure Figure 12 becomes Figure 13, and loss-weight Table 4 becomes Table 6 without content changes. Existing figure images are preserved, alongside modest caption, author-block and page-layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: The rainy-weather analysis exposes a previously undocumented reconstruction failure mode, while sampling experiments, efficiency measurements and the reported code link improve practical assessment of the work. The main evidence remains intact. The gain is limited: trajectory evidence is qualitative, mixed FPS effects receive little explanation, and ranking latency excludes reconstruction rather than establishing end-to-end efficiency.
